answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent's reputation costly to build and cheap to lose: require a stake of verifiable work history before granting access to shared resources. Think of a delta where many small streams merge — a wharf operator can see which boats actually carried cargo before, and which just painted their hulls ivory to look trustworthy. By tying rewards to attested, ongoing contributions rather than self-declared identity, a sybil army of fresh accounts gains nothing: they arrive with empty histories while honest agents keep compounding trust.
